raw_review_excerpt:
The plan's final round adds an 'Ownership Discovery Checkpoint' that identifies Mase's shared my-oss-fork-manager as the canonical reusable owner, documents a real registry-vs-marker mirror-branch mismatch, and commits (pre-Slice-2) to replacing direct apply with a durable-artifact/exact-SHA/--apply gate and to stripping automatic rebase --abort/reset --hard recovery from the shared apply path. All four focus claims are grounded in the actual shared-owner script, registry, and marker files. No BLOCK-level freeze-safety defect found; two WARN items remain around handoff clarity and an unresolved policy direction, both explicitly gated on before implementation begins.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] Slice 1 duplicates work the checkpoint already performed
- 2. [WARN] Mirror-policy normalization direction is unspecified
- 3. [NOTE] Track A completion gate is a hard external dependency not independently re-verified this round
closure_verification: All four carried items from the prior round are addressed at the plan-text level: two (shared-owner identification, durable-intake-artifact contract) are fully resolved as design commitments; two (mirror-policy mismatch, automatic rebase-abort/reset-hard recovery) are correctly and transparently flagged as still-open in the actual code/config, with explicit pre-Slice-2 gating rather than false claims of completion. This is the expected and safe disposition for a plan-gate review at 'refinement-required' status — no BLOCK remains against the plan document itself.

prior_round_closure.title: Graphify mirror-policy mismatch between registry, marker, and docs
prior_round_closure.caller_claim: Plan documents the mismatch (registry expects a missing 'upstream-v8' mirror while the marker declares 'mirror/upstream-v8') and gates Slice 2 on normalizing it.
prior_round_closure.verification_notes: The mismatch is real and confirmed directly from registry.json vs the marker file vs AGENTS.md. The plan appropriately discloses it and gates future implementation on fixing it, but the underlying inconsistency itself remains unresolved in the repo, and the plan does not yet state which value should win.

prior_round_closure.title: Durable intake artifact contract undefined
prior_round_closure.caller_claim: Phase 1 and Slice 2 now specify an explicit --output path requirement, atomic write, and default no-overwrite behavior for the intake artifact.
prior_round_closure.verification_notes: The plan text now specifies enough contract detail (explicit output path required for durability, atomic write, refuse-overwrite default, schema fields for command versions/SHAs/timestamp/outcomes) to be actionable at design-review level; current shared-owner code only prints JSON to stdout today, consistent with this being correctly scoped as not-yet-built work.

prior_round_closure.title: Automatic rebase --abort / reset --hard recovery incompatible with Graphify's no-auto-recovery requirement
prior_round_closure.caller_claim: Plan commits to removing this behavior from the apply path before Slice 2 begins.
prior_round_closure.verification_notes: Confirmed the behavior is real and currently present: ForkAdapter._update_failure_recovery (inherited by GraphifyAdapter) runs 'git rebase --abort' on rebase failure and 'git reset --hard'/'git update-ref' during validation-failure recovery. The plan correctly identifies this as a pre-Slice-2 removal requirement rather than falsely claiming it is already fixed, which is the appropriate honest disposition for a plan document, but the unsafe behavior itself has not yet been removed from the code.

issues.title: Slice 1 duplicates work the checkpoint already performed
issues.details: Autonomous Execution Slices > Slice 1, steps 1-2 ask a future agent to 'Inventory the global OSS fork-manager instructions... Determine whether a shared owner already has an intake/artifact format' and 'Record the ownership-discovery result before any Slice 2 work.' The Ownership Discovery Checkpoint at the bottom of the document already executed this exact step on 2026-07-13 and recorded 'found shared owner' with exact paths. The plan does not mark Slice 1 steps 1-2 as satisfied, which could cause a future implementer to redo discovery or wonder whether the checkpoint superseded the slice instructions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note in Slice 1 (or at the top of the checkpoint) stating that steps 1-2 are satisfied by the Ownership Discovery Checkpoint below, and that Slice 1 execution should begin at step 3 (adapter-boundary inspection) unless the shared-owner facts change before implementation.

issues.title: Mirror-policy normalization direction is unspecified
issues.details: The checkpoint correctly identifies that the registry declares mirror='upstream-v8' while the repo marker (and AGENTS.md, which says 'Keep local mirror branches such as mirror/upstream-v8 clean') declares mirror='mirror/upstream-v8'. The plan's refinement item 1 says only to 'normalize the Graphify mirror policy across registry, marker, and docs' without stating which convention should win or who decides. Two of three sources (marker, AGENTS.md) already agree on 'mirror/upstream-v8', suggesting the registry is the stale one, but the plan doesn't say so.
issues.suggested_fix: State a directional default (e.g., 'the registry.json mirror field for graphify should be corrected to mirror/upstream-v8 to match the marker and AGENTS.md unless Mase decides otherwise') so Slice 1 has a concrete default instead of an open-ended normalization task.

issues.title: Track A completion gate is a hard external dependency not independently re-verified this round
issues.details: The plan correctly treats Track A (semantic CLI reconciliation recovery) as a hard prerequisite and states its status is unresolved. This review did not open the Track A plan document to confirm its current validation state, since it is out of this round's scoped focus (shared-owner ownership, mirror-policy, durable intake, automatic-recovery prohibition).
issues.suggested_fix: No plan-text change needed; this is a disclosure for the reader, not a defect. Confirm Track A's validation-clean status via its own gate before authorizing any Slice 2/3 work under this plan.

verification_gaps: The 'codex reconcile' dry-run/--apply scope-boundary claim in the Decision Boundary section was not independently re-verified against graphify/cli.py this round (only 1 line was read).
docs/mase-fork-operating-model.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, both cited as authoritative context in 'Verified Starting State', were not opened this round to confirm they still say what the plan claims.

Whether the checkout is currently dirty and mase/local-fixes truly diverges from origin (as the checkpoint claims) could not be independently confirmed with the tools available in this review session (no shell/git access).
recommended_fixes: Mark Slice 1 steps 1-2 as already satisfied by the Ownership Discovery Checkpoint to avoid duplicate rediscovery work.
State a default direction for the mirror-branch naming conflict (registry vs marker/AGENTS.md) so Slice 1 has an unambiguous default to apply pending Mase's sign-off.
workflow_compliance: Plan correctly separates read-only intake (Phase 1) from explicit mutation (Phase 2), matching the shared-owner's actual update-plan/update-apply split found in code.
Plan defers implementation until the shared-owner ownership question is resolved, which it now demonstrably is (GraphifyAdapter exists, tested, registered).

Plan explicitly gates Slice 2 start on resolving the mirror-policy mismatch and removing automatic rebase --abort/reset --hard recovery, both of which are confirmed to be real, currently-present conditions rather than hypothetical risks.
technical_reality: GraphifyAdapter(ForkAdapter) in adapters/base.py inherits _standard_update_apply, which currently runs 'git rebase --abort' on rebase failure and 'git reset --hard' plus 'git update-ref' during validation-failure recovery (lines ~1157-1198 of base.py) — this is the exact automatic recovery behavior the plan commits to removing before Slice 2.

registry.json declares graphify branches.mirror = 'upstream-v8'; the repo's own guardrail marker (.codex/oss-fork-manager.json) declares branches.mirror = 'mirror/upstream-v8'; AGENTS.md independently corroborates the marker's 'mirror/upstream-v8' naming — confirming the registry is the outlier needing correction.
test_contracts.py imports ArchonAdapter, GraphifyAdapter, GsdAdapter directly from adapters.base, confirming the adapter and its test coverage are real, not just described in the plan.

The shared owner's update-fork command supports a read-only --handoff mode and a separate --approved apply path with explicit denial when neither is set, matching the plan's Phase 1/Phase 2 split already partially built into the shared owner.
assumptions_to_verify: That the checkout is currently dirty and mase/local-fixes diverges from origin as the checkpoint states (not independently confirmed via git in this tool-constrained review session).
That graphify/cli.py's 'codex reconcile' command truly has a separate, already-existing dry-run/--apply contract distinct from this plan's target process (only 1 line of cli.py was read this round).
That docs/mase-fork-operating-model.md and ARCHITECTURE.md still contain the release-review/adoption-category/staged-canary/operator-briefing content the plan attributes to them.
verification_sufficiency: Sufficient: all four explicitly scoped focus claims (shared-owner ownership, mirror-policy mismatch, durable-intake-artifact design, automatic reset/abort prohibition) were checked against real code/config files, not just narrative.

Insufficient: broader campaign context (Track A status, operating-model doc, ARCHITECTURE.md, adoption.py/install.py, full cli.py) was not re-read this round; treat those as carried-forward assumptions rather than re-verified facts.
downstream_risks: If Slice 1 is executed without noticing the Ownership Discovery Checkpoint already answered steps 1-2, an implementer could waste effort or, worse, second-guess the already-confirmed shared-owner location.

If the mirror-policy normalization is resolved in the wrong direction (e.g., someone 'fixes' the marker/AGENTS.md to match the registry's 'upstream-v8' instead of the reverse), it would silently diverge from the two sources that already agree, compounding the confusion this plan is trying to remove.

The automatic rebase --abort/reset --hard recovery in the shared owner's base ForkAdapter is also inherited by GsdAdapter and the generic adapter path used by other forks (Archon, agent-skills); removing or gating it only for Graphify (as this plan implies) could leave the same unsafe recovery behavior live for other managed forks unless the shared-owner fix is applied at the ForkAdapter base-class level with fork-aware exceptions, not a Graphify-only patch.
review.freeze_recommendation: Safe to freeze. Carry the remaining WARN/NOTE items as explicit follow-ups or implementation-time checks.
